INITIALIZATION OF THE FINE SYSTEM The constrained Monte Carlo is an irreducible, aperiodic, and detailed balanced Markov chain and, as a result, even a randomly initialized configuration of the fine system is mathematically guaranteed to converge to the conditional probability distribution p(φ|Φ), where p(Φ|φ) is the forward transformation. Nevertheless, we can efficiently initialize the fine lattice, close to equilibrium. We clarify that constrained Monte Carlo can be conveniently parallelized with a sublattice decomposition, in which simultaneously updated sites are neither nearest neighbors nor contained in a common kernel. We assign to each block BX in the fine system a constant field φx = uX whose smeared value approximately inverts the transformation.
